author: Isaac Newton

alt_text: An old, slightly stained parchment title page of Sir Isaac Newton's book, 'Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica,' printed in 1687. The Latin text is printed in a classic serif font inside a simple double-bordered rectangular frame, featuring the book's title prominently at the top, followed by Newton's name, an official printing approval signed by Samuel Pepys dated 1686, and the publication details for London in Roman numerals at the bottom.

label: The Paleolithic Era (Early Counting Marks)
BCE to CE transition
The Great Pyramid of Giza is completed in Egypt, standing as the world's tallest man-made structure for over 3,800 years.
Enheduanna is appointed High Priestess of Ur in Mesopotamia, becoming the earliest individual author recorded by name in human history.
The Code of Hammurabi is enacted in Babylon, establishing one of the earliest and most complete surviving written legal codes.
Hatshepsut ascends the throne as Pharaoh of Egypt, initiating a period marked by peace, prolific monumental architecture, and vast regional trade.
The Han Dynasty establishes formal trade routes to the West, opening the Silk Road and initiating centuries of Eurasian cultural and economic exchange.
The Trưng Sisters lead a military uprising against Han Dynasty rule, briefly establishing an autonomous state in ancient Vietnam.
The court official Cai Lun standardises the plant-fibre papermaking process in China, fundamentally altering global administration and record-keeping.
The mathematician, astronomer, and Neoplatonist philosopher Hypatia dies in Alexandria during a period of intense socio-political unrest.
Empress Wu Zetian officially proclaims the Wu Zhou Dynasty, becoming the only female monarch to rule China in her own right.
The city of Baghdad is founded, rapidly expanding into a prominent intellectual and scientific capital during the Islamic Golden Age.
Norse mariners establish a settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in modern-day Canada, representing the earliest known European transatlantic voyage.
King John of England seals the Magna Carta, establishing the legal precedent that the monarch is subject to the rule of law.
The Mexica people found the city of Tenochtitlan, establishing the geopolitical foundation for the expansion of the Aztec Empire.
Maritime trade routes bring the second plague pandemic to Europe via Sicily, altering the demographic and economic structure of the continent.
Joan of Arc successfully relieves the Siege of Orléans, shifting the strategic momentum of the Hundred Years' War in favour of France.
Johannes Gutenberg develops the movable-type printing press in Germany, introducing a system of mass communication to Europe.
A maritime expedition commanded by Christopher Columbus arrives in the Caribbean, initiating sustained interaction between Europe and the Americas.
The vessel Victoria returns to Spain under the command of Juan Sebastián Elcano, completing the first documented global circumnavigation.
Queen Nzinga becomes ruler of Ndongo in modern Angola, directing prolonged military and diplomatic strategies against colonial expansion.
James Watt introduces his refined commercial steam engine, providing the mechanical foundation for the Industrial Revolution.
The storming of the Bastille takes place in Paris, marking a major turning point in the French Revolution and the decline of absolute monarchies.
The British Parliament enacts the Slave Trade Act, marking a significant legal step toward the eventual global prohibition of the transatlantic slave trade.
Ada Lovelace completes her technical notes on the Analytical Engine, creating the first complex algorithm intended for machine execution.
Harriet Tubman escapes bondage and begins a decade-long series of rescue missions to guide enslaved people along the Underground Railroad.
Marie Curie is co-awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for her research on radiation, becoming the first female recipient of a Nobel Prize.
Suffragists march on the British Parliament and encounter severe police resistance, marking a pivotal escalation in the global campaign for women's suffrage.
Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia, initiating World War I and ending a century of relative geopolitical stability among major European powers.
Rosa Parks refuses to surrender her seat on a segregated bus in Alabama, acting as a catalyst for the Montgomery bus boycott and the civil rights movement.
Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launches into orbit aboard Vostok 6, becoming the first woman to travel in space.
The research scientist Tu Youyou isolates artemisinin in China, yielding a breakthrough antimalarial therapy that significantly lowered global mortality rates.
The opening of the Berlin Wall begins, initiating the collapse of Eastern Bloc regimes and symbolising the approaching conclusion of the Cold War.
